svg.title: Nail puller lever
svg.desc: The hand pushes down with F_i at the long handle. The puller rests directly on the plank at the pivot, which supplies upward N. The nail pushes down on the claw with F_n. Horizontal perpendicular arms l_i and l_o straddle the pivot, with l_i much longer. The dashed upward F_o acts on the nail, not on the puller, and equals F_n in magnitude. The separate free-body diagram includes only the three forces on the puller. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A lever gains force by moving its input farther than its output
Red: on lever; green: on nail; blue: pivot reaction
F in (N)
F out (N)

Ideal rigid lever, vertical endpoint forces, arm lengths 0.60 and 0.10 m. Endpoint arcs are schematic
nail-puller motion; readouts use vertical travel. F in Δy in = F out Δy out.
